newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey cabinet meeting postponed in Islamist row.
newsitem.headline: Turkey cabinet meeting postponed in Islamist row.

text.p: A meeting of Turkey's Islamist-led cabinet was postponed on Tuesday amid a row between the coalition partners over Islamist activism, a spokesman for Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan said.
"The cabinet meeting due for today was called off," the spokesman told Reuters. The cabinet has not met for eight weeks in a deepening government rift.

Four anti-Islamist MPs from Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller's True Path Party have resigned in recent days, reducing the government's majority on paper to only one, although vacant seats give it a larger margin.
Army pressure on Erbakan, Turkey's first Islamist prime minister, has brought the 11-month-old coalition close to breaking point.
The generals have demanded a crackdown on Islamist activism that Erbakan is reluctant to deliver.
The government faces the prospect of another opposition censure within two weeks after narrowly surviving a censure bid last week.
